- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and underperform when sentiment is negative or neutral (e.g., <0.3).  
- Avoid sharp upward spikes in forecast after recent price increases; model tends to overreact and overshoot.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (e.g., alternating 0.3–0.7), reduce forecast volatility and favor mean reversion toward recent 10–15 day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, cap forecast growth to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is consistently low or negative, model tends to underestimate — adjust downward by 2–5% of recent average.  
- Forecast should not lag sentiment trends by more than 2–3 days; if sentiment turns sharply, model should adjust within 1–2 days.  
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or slightly declining, model often overcorrects upward — reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overbought bias.
